observations.statement: History pooling improves AUC over static features by 0.0052224992242449, and target-aware attention improves over pooling by 0.0031358724110028. Both changes also lower overall Logloss. History and target conditioning therefore have local predictive value under this recipe.

Both ordinary arms reproduce their corresponding ancestors exactly in aggregate AUC, Logloss, and every reported slice metric, at identical parameter counts. This supports use of the ordinary arms as bridges for intervention attribution.

Full count correction lowers AUC and raises Logloss in both branches. The pooled penalty is -0.0017334134126946 AUC / +0.0000367396712915 Logloss; the DIN penalty is -0.0001905059724607 AUC / +0.0000314515662284 Logloss.
observations.outcome: negative for the proposed full-correction performance benefit

observations.statement: The AUC difference-in-differences is +0.0015429074402339. Target-aware scoring substantially attenuates the correction penalty in this seed; it does not reverse the overall ranking.

The diagnostic intervention is active: at the ordinary DIN checkpoint, mean pv attention mass conditional on pv presence changes from 0.829869 under ordinary weights to 0.323921 under corrected weights. The corrected-trained checkpoint has 0.965264 under ordinary counterfactual weights and 0.673296 under its active corrected weights. These are two normalizations per checkpoint; cross-checkpoint differences also include learned representation changes. Per-type reported means use different presence-conditioned denominators and must not be summed as a probability partition.
observations.scope: Candidate-supplied, first 512 validation impressions, not independently verified

observations.statement: Diagnostics cover 4 empty, 40 single-type and 468 mixed-type histories; 395/468 mixed histories have at least 90% pv events. Padding mass is zero and maximum normalization error is at most 2.3842e-7. Single-type summary perturbation is about 3e-7 to 4e-7 for DIN, consistent with subtracting a common log-count leaving softmax weights invariant. This is a narrow implementation sanity check, not population evidence or a relevance assessment.

Corrected DIN gains +0.0003955323 AUC on category_match_absent (717,129 samples / 29,616 positives / 687,513 negatives), while Logloss worsens by +0.0000537532; category_match_present loses -0.0003253239 AUC. The diagnostic category-absent subset also includes 16 brand-present histories among 134 nonempty category-absent histories. Category absence cannot be interpreted as absence of all useful evidence.

Corrected DIN loses -0.0015670382 AUC for history_1_16 and -0.0009893867 for history_17_64, but only -0.0000234989 for history_gt64. The longest slice contains 93.5849% of validation impressions. Global AUC includes cross-slice positive-negative pairs, so it cannot be decomposed as a sample-weighted sum of slice AUCs.

On empty histories corrected DIN improves +0.0019564707 AUC and -0.0017289143 Logloss, although the normalization has no direct event-weight intervention there. The 8,272 impressions contain only 310 positives. End-to-end retraining changes shared parameters, so empty/single-type cross-model changes do not establish a direct normalization effect.

Corrected DIN worsens AUC in the four supplied frequency groups below 100 and improves it by +0.0006541180 in the highest-frequency group, where Logloss worsens +0.0000913672. No calibration or frequency-specific mechanism is established by these aggregate divergences.

All seven supplied trials have success status and null errors. There is no supplied execution-failure or abandoned-implementation receipt. The unsuccessful scientific branches are full correction in pooling and full correction in DIN; they remain in the analysis. Baseline and bridge reruns use the same seed and do not constitute independent support.

observations.statement: The static, pooled and target-aware references have AUC 0.6050036145, 0.6102261137 and 0.6133619861. Pooling and target conditioning each improve both overall metrics at seed 42. Ordinary round-one controls exactly reproduce the corresponding reported reference metrics and slices.

All nine supplied trials succeeded operationally, including both latest arms. Full correction is a negative performance trajectory, not a failed execution: AUC falls by 0.0017334134 for pooling and 0.0001905060 for DIN, with worse Logloss in both. No failed execution receipt or additional abandoned branch is supplied.

Latest half-corrected pooling reaches AUC 0.6108065192 and Logloss 0.1969882654: changes of +0.0005804055 and -0.0000981980 against ordinary pooling. It recovers and exceeds the full-correction pooling penalty, but remains below ordinary DIN by 0.0025554669 AUC and has higher Logloss.

Latest half-corrected DIN reaches AUC 0.6131537618 and Logloss 0.1968125047: changes of -0.0002082243 and +0.0000178582 against ordinary DIN. Against full correction, AUC is lower by 0.0000177184 while Logloss improves by 0.0000135933. Thus half strength does not rescue the primary DIN objective in this seed.

The attention-by-correction AUC interaction is +0.0015429074 at full strength but -0.0007886299 at half strength. The original positive interaction does not extend uniformly over strength. DIN has a relatively flat three-point response while pooling is nonmonotonic; three points do not identify an optimum or response curve.

Latest candidate-supplied first-512 diagnostics show active alpha=0.5, zero padding mass, weight-sum error at most 2.3842e-7, zero empty summary, and near-invariant conditional within-type weights and single-type weights. Mixed-history mean half-versus-ordinary summary L2 changes are 1.0636960 for pooling and 1.1264205 for DIN. These support an active between-type redistribution in this limited sample, not a causal performance explanation.

At the half-DIN checkpoint, mean pv mass conditional on pv presence is 0.9295267 under ordinary normalization, 0.7707562 under half, and 0.4762428 under full correction. The corresponding half-pooling values are 0.9447256, 0.7888888 and 0.4281723. These are same-checkpoint counterfactual normalizations, not three retrained model performance measurements. Type-specific means use different presence denominators and must not be summed.

The diagnostic sample contains 4 empty, 40 single-type and 468 mixed-type histories; 395 mixed histories have at least 90% pv share. It is the first 512 ordered impressions, not a random population sample. Raw DIN score means differ across trained checkpoints and are not comparable evidence of compensation without centered, matched-input analysis.

Half pooling improves AUC and Logloss in each of four hour bins, but not every slice: past-buy-present AUC and the lowest user-frequency AUC decline. In category-match-absent impressions its AUC increases by 0.0009956346 while Logloss worsens by 0.0000363654. Half DIN instead loses category-absent AUC by 0.0004225199, reversing the full-DIN exploratory gain of 0.0003955323; Logloss worsens for both corrected DIN strengths in that slice.

Half DIN improves empty-history AUC by 0.0048421535 and Logloss by 0.0009431824 despite zero empty summaries in diagnostics. Such changes can arise through shared parameter training; they cannot be attributed to direct reweighting of empty histories. The slice has only 310 positive exposures. All three nonempty length bins have lower half-DIN AUC than ordinary DIN.

All six normalization arms report 17,130,275 parameters, including the unused attention module in pooling controls. Half pooling uses 455.44 training seconds and 430,361,088 peak GPU bytes; half DIN uses 491.36 seconds and 654,937,600 bytes. This is a matched-recipe/capacity comparison, not measured equal compute. Shorter round-two times occur in both branches and do not establish a correction-specific speedup.

observations.statement: Pooling improves AUC over static by 0.0052224992, and target-aware attention adds 0.0031358724 over pooling. Both also lower Logloss. This establishes useful histories and target conditioning for the local references; it does not identify a query or field bottleneck.

Full count correction loses AUC in pooling (-0.0017334134) and DIN (-0.0001905060), and worsens Logloss in both. Half correction improves pooling (+0.0005804055 AUC, -0.0000981980 Logloss) but loses DIN AUC (-0.0002082243). Half DIN is also below full DIN AUC. These operationally successful negative interventions must be retained.

The attention-by-count-correction AUC interaction changes from +0.0015429074 at full strength to -0.0007886299 at half strength. Frequent-type mass and summaries change in diagnostics, yet usefulness is branch dependent. This qualifies the older attention-compensation explanation.

All 13 supplied model trials report success and null errors. No failed model execution is exposed. Scientific negatives, missing inputs, preparation/source-access failures and successful host training are different statuses.

The latest joint restriction has AUC 0.6144940344 and Logloss 0.1966904258. Relative to the latest ordinary product, changes are +0.0011629547 AUC and -0.0001788009 Logloss; relative to historical DIN, +0.0011320483 and -0.0001042207. These are single-seed validation results.

Removing cross products alone improves both metrics at either context setting: AUC +0.0009657589 with context retained and +0.0006829896 with context removed; Logloss -0.0001967024 and -0.0003059556. Context removal improves AUC at either cross setting (+0.0004799650 and +0.0001971958), but worsens Logloss (+0.0001271547 and +0.0000179014). The cross-removal arm has the best Logloss among the four latest arms.

The cross-by-context AUC interaction is -0.0002827692: the joint AUC gain is subadditive, not positive synergy. The Logloss interaction is -0.0001092532, favorable on the lower-is-better scale, but context removal still increases Logloss at both settings. The interaction does not eliminate the joint-versus-cross Logloss tradeoff.

The ordinary-product bridge differs from historical DIN by -0.0000309064 AUC and +0.0000745803 Logloss. Slice differences are larger in some small groups; empty-history AUC differs by +0.0028066785. Exact source/operation-equivalence assertions in submission notes are not established by the supplied host outcomes.

Latest diagnostics show declared factor flags, zero padding mass and zero empty summaries, weight normalization error at most 1.78814e-7, and product decomposition relative error at most 3.93581e-7. These are candidate-authored checks on the first 512 ordered validation impressions, not independent full-population certification.

At the ordinary-product checkpoint, removing cross products changes mean attention L1 by 0.4398596, history-summary L2 by 1.1341075 and absolute logit by 0.0782455 over nonempty diagnostic examples. The joint change gives 0.5811910, 1.5538177 and 0.1084849. Both category-match and brand-match mass rise under that joint counterfactual. This shows numerical activity at a fixed checkpoint; no counterfactual full-validation predictive score is supplied.

The diagnostic subset has 508 nonempty and 4 empty impressions, 374 category matches, 145 brand matches, 129 both, 245 category-only, 16 brand-only and 118 neither. There are 51 target-brand-zero impressions and no zero target categories. Match-mass means condition on different sets and cannot be summed or interpreted as relevance labels.

The joint arm improves AUC and Logloss in all four reported hour bins and both category-match slices relative to the latest ordinary arm, but loses both metrics in empty-history and pv-absent slices. Empty: 8272 exposures/310 positives, delta AUC -0.0021201514, delta Logloss +0.0004096582; pv-absent: 10998/397, delta AUC -0.0022802136, delta Logloss +0.0008753525. These overlapping exploratory groups do not justify a gate.

The joint arm gains AUC and lowers Logloss in all three nonempty length bins; history_gt64 contains 3026583 of 3234051 impressions. It is not universally strongest within slices: cross removal has better Logloss in several groups and better AUC in the two lowest reported user-frequency bins. Overall AUC cannot be reconstructed by averaging slice AUC.

All latest arms have 17130275 parameters (17078688 embedding; 51587 dense). Their training times span 505.87 to 526.05 seconds, wall times 593.72 to 614.37, and peak GPU bytes 801711616 to 828414464. Joint versus ordinary uses slightly more wall/train time and nearly equal peak memory. Relative to historical DIN, memory rises from 654936064 to 802390016 bytes. Timing/memory include differing code or diagnostic execution conditions; no equal-compute or speedup claim follows.

prior_work_and_difference.inherited_components: Per receipts: embeddings, category/brand/action/recency histories, target-aware scorer, masked softmax, history values, classifier and training recipe. Source files are not exposed for independent verification.
prior_work_and_difference.reported_local_mechanism: Let q=target-category + target-brand and h_i=history-category + history-brand + action/recency context. In the explicit product block, ordinary q*h_i decomposes into D_i (same-field category/category and brand/brand), X_i (the two off-diagonal category/brand products), and C_i (target times action/recency). The factorial block is D_i+(1-A)X_i+(1-B)C_i. Products are elementwise; exact embedding assembly is receipt-inferred, not source-inspected. The joint retains only D_i in this block. Other scorer blocks and values still carry context and allow learned interactions.
prior_work_and_difference.difference_from_count_branch: Earlier work modifies between-type attention normalization s_i-alpha*log(n_type). The latest branch changes explicit product construction at fixed declared normalized aggregation. No evidence estimates combining the two interventions, and their results must not be pooled as one factor.

Same-checkpoint attention perturbations differ from retrained-model performance. Changes in match mass, norms or logits establish numerical activity only, and cross-checkpoint changes conflate retraining.

Empty (310 positives), pv-absent (397) and frequency-1_2 (1045) particularly lack strong independent support. Slice sets overlap; many comparisons invite selection bias.

The 128-event window prevents claims about omitted histories or unavailable item IDs. Static user/ad snapshot as-of dates are undocumented, so production point-in-time validity remains unverified under the preserved benchmark assumption.

observations.statement: Baseline histories are useful: pooled minus static AUC is +0.0052224992; DIN minus pooled is +0.0031358724, with lower Logloss in both. This does not isolate a field/query bottleneck.

Full count correction loses AUC and Logloss in both pooling and DIN. Half correction improves pooling (+0.0005804055 AUC) but reduces DIN AUC (-0.0002082243), slightly below full-corrected DIN. The bounded partial-correction follow-up did not rescue the target-aware branch.

Round-3 joint restriction leads primary validation AUC at 0.6144940344272417, Logloss 0.19669042580912716. It improves AUC by 0.0011629546942916394 over its ordinary adapter and 0.0011320483081733723 over historical DIN. Relative to historical DIN Logloss falls by 0.00010422066570520139.

Cross-field removal improves both metrics at either context setting. Context-product removal increases AUC but worsens Logloss at either cross setting. Joint minus cross-only AUC is +0.00019719580032073747 and Logloss is +0.000017901439788470253. Thus cross-only is a consequential comparator and both restrictions are not required for an improvement.
The 2x2 AUC interaction is -0.00028276924606862597: joint gains are subadditive. The Logloss interaction is -0.00010925323629681905 on a lower-is-better scale. No positive AUC synergy is supported.

Round 4 exactly reproduces each historical path's reported AUC, Logloss and all slice counts/metrics: historical baseline, ordinary adapter and joint adapter. The baseline-adapter offset persists at -0.00003090638611826746 AUC and +0.00007458025739059175 Logloss. Replays narrow the explanation toward a stable implementation/training-path difference; they do not identify its cause or certify source equivalence.

The new inline joint realization exactly matches the adapter joint's reported AUC, Logloss, every reported slice, and all 57 common diagnostic keys. Its extra inline_helper_logit_abs_max is 0 on the first 512 validation impressions. This supports limited implementation consistency. It is neither a new mechanism nor an independent seed.

The inline joint versus original inline baseline therefore retains the +0.0011320483 AUC gain in an alternative implementation path reported to follow the baseline forward structure. This weakens an explanation attributing the entire gain solely to the ordinary adapter's mismatch, conditional on receipt-described isolation. Unexposed source and training traces prevent a full audit.

Candidate-authored diagnostics show active attention/summary/logit changes under same-checkpoint product interventions, with zero padding mass/empty summary, normalization errors <=1.78814e-7 and product-decomposition errors <=3.93581e-7 in the product quartet. These measure numerical activity on 512 ordered impressions, not semantic relevance or causal mediation of the score gain.

Joint improves both metrics against the ordinary adapter in all nonempty length bins, four hour bins, category-match bins, and reported frequency bins. It loses both metrics in empty_history (8272/310 positives) and past_pv_absent (10998/397 positives). Those losses recur exactly in round-4 replays, which add no independent subgroup support. Against historical baseline the empty-history AUC direction differs (+0.0006865271), while Logloss still worsens; subgroup claims depend on the comparator.

All compared history models have 17130275 parameters: 17078688 embedding and 51587 dense. Inline joint peak allocation is 738064384 bytes versus adapter joint 802390016 (-64325632, approximately 8.0%), but exceeds inline baseline's 654936064. Inline joint training/wall time is 519.64/611.16 seconds versus adapter replay 527.97/620.68; this is one timing comparison with different diagnostic paths, not an equal-compute efficiency result.

All 17 exposed trajectory entries report execution success; the 15 direct detailed receipts have null errors. The two missing detailed pooling receipts are supplemented from scoped prior memory, with current index confirmation of status/AUC/wall time. No failed host model execution is exposed. Negative count-correction results are scientific negatives, not missing data or execution failures.

observations.statement: Pooled history improves AUC over static features by 0.0052224992; target-aware history adds 0.0031358724 over pooling. Both reduce Logloss. This establishes useful baseline history signal, not a specific semantic matching mechanism.

Full count correction hurts both pooling and DIN. Half correction helps pooling (+0.0005804055 AUC) but not DIN (-0.0002082243); full-corrected DIN is also below ordinary (-0.0001905060). The bounded partial-correction follow-up did not rescue the target-aware branch. All are successful executions with scientific negative outcomes, not failed jobs.

In round 3, removing explicit cross-field products improves both metrics at either context setting. Context-product removal raises AUC but worsens Logloss at either cross setting. The AUC interaction is negative (-0.0002827692), so the joint gain is subadditive. Both restrictions are not necessary for an improvement.

Round-4 replays exactly match their source paths on all reported aggregate and slice metrics. Inline joint matches adapter joint, with zero helper logit discrepancy on the first 512 impressions. Original baseline and ordinary adapter remain different (-0.0000309064 adapter AUC, +0.0000745803 Logloss). This is stable seed-42 path dependence without identified root cause.

Latest normalized aligned candidate has AUC 0.6149816911798147 and Logloss 0.19656340759133067 on 3,234,051 validation exposures (159,437 positives). It leads all 20 supplied trial entries in AUC and all 20 recovered detailed rows in Logloss; repeated rows do not supply independent support.

Aligned normalization improves AUC by 0.0004876568 and reduces Logloss by 0.0001270182 versus raw aligned. Crossed normalization changes AUC by only +0.0000139449 and worsens Logloss by +0.0002459431. A universal benefit from product normalization is not observed.

Aligned beats crossed by +0.0011162489 AUC with raw products and +0.0015899607 with unit products; Logloss also favors aligned in both. Alignment-by-normalization AUC interaction is +0.0004737118 and Logloss interaction -0.0003729613. This differs from round-3 subadditivity because the factors are different.

Latest-minus-original-DIN AUC is +0.0016197051 and Logloss -0.0002312389; latest also improves both metrics versus the earlier context-retaining cross-removal arm. The aggregate AUC/Logloss tradeoff between the earlier joint and context-retaining restriction is no longer a reason to prefer either over the latest candidate at seed 42.

Latest supplied diagnostics report unit product norm 1.0, maximum unit norm error 1.78814e-7, aligned/crossed unit norm difference <=2.38419e-7, zero padding mass, zero empty summary and zero forward/helper logit error on the first 512 impressions. All 60,475 visible valid events are nonfloored in both products. Unit aligned/crossed directions differ (mean cosines -0.02531, +0.00495, -0.00628 in the three trained checkpoints).

Normalization at the aligned-unit checkpoint changes weights, summaries and logits relative to aligned-raw counterfactuals (mean nonempty weight L1 1.59829, summary L2 5.57161, absolute logit change 0.45850). These are diagnostic activity measurements, not counterfactual validation scores or causal mediation. All diagnostic variants are referenced to aligned raw, not each checkpoint active model.

Latest improves both metrics over raw aligned in 21 of 23 supplied slices, but loses both in history_17_64 (157391 samples/6311 positives) and user_train_frequency_100_4294967296 (1004912/33140). It improves AUC and Logloss over original DIN in all 23 slices. It beats crossed-unit AUC in all 23, but has worse Logloss in empty_history, past_pv_absent and the highest frequency bin. These are exploratory overlapping summaries.

Latest recovers the raw-aligned empty-history and pv-absent losses, but zero history summaries mean empty-history changes cannot directly demonstrate better history-event matching; training of shared representations/classifier can change these scores.

All history arms report 17,130,275 parameters (17,078,688 embedding; 51,587 dense). Latest wall/train times are 614.783/524.601 seconds, peak GPU allocation 832,739,328 bytes, throughput 179,887.75 examples/s and whole-batch p95 22.135 ms at batch size 4096 including feature gathering. Latest versus raw aligned increases peak allocation 3.78% and train time 1.94%; versus original DIN increases peak allocation 27.15% with similar train time. Single-run timing does not establish an efficiency frontier.

All 20 trajectory entries report operational success; all 15 directly supplied detailed receipts have null errors. Five older detailed receipts are available only in scoped agent-r0004 memory and are marked as such. No failed host model run is exposed, and no unseen failure is invented.

prior_work_and_difference.local_algebra: Let q_c,q_b be target category/brand vectors; h_c,h_b history category/brand vectors; u action/recency context. D=q_c*h_c+q_b*h_b (aligned), X=q_c*h_b+q_b*h_c (crossed), C=(q_c+q_b)*u, with * elementwise. Ordinary product block is D+X+C. Round-3 flags form D+(1-A)X+(1-B)C. r0003-cross_only REMOVES X and retains D+C; it is NOT the r0005 crossed replacement, which uses X alone. r0003-context_only removes C and retains D+X. Raw aligned is D; latest unit aligned normalizes D by its per-event L2 norm with an implementation floor; crossed arms replace D by X with raw or unit normalization. Exact floor constant/source is not exposed. Other scorer blocks and history values retain context and learned mixed-field interactions.
prior_work_and_difference.mechanism_difference: Count correction changes s_i to s_i-alpha*log(n_type), affecting between-type attention mass. Product restriction/replacement instead changes one explicit target-history interaction block. Unit normalization changes that block magnitude and gradients; it is neither count balancing nor softmax removal. No supplied trial combines these mechanisms.

observations.observation: All 23 supplied model trajectories succeeded operationally. Full count correction loses AUC for pooling (-0.0017334134) and DIN (-0.0001905060). Half correction improves pooling (+0.0005804055) but loses DIN AUC (-0.0002082243). Half pooling remains below DIN. These are negative or limited scientific outcomes, not failed execution.

Round-3 joint product restriction improved AUC over its ordinary adapter by 0.0011629547; removing cross-field products alone nearly matched it. The joint version had slightly worse Logloss than the cross-field-removal-only arm. Round-4 replays preserved the reported outcomes, while baseline versus ordinary adapter retained a small numerical-path discrepancy. This supports local behavior, not universal benefit from both removals.

The round-6 same-body aligned/raw bridge exactly reproduces historical raw aligned AUC, Logloss and every supplied slice metric/count at seed 42. Its source hash differs. This narrows the earlier mixed-round raw-corner uncertainty at the outcome level; source and backward identity remain unverified.

Full-gradient normalized aligned remains the validation incumbent: AUC 0.6149816911798147, Logloss 0.19656340759133067. Detached aligned reaches AUC 0.6145833321081287, Logloss 0.19663658831646288. Full-minus-detached is +0.00039835907168606077 AUC and -0.0000731807251322103 Logloss. Detached aligned still beats aligned raw by +0.00008929768088694612 AUC and -0.00005383749266427151 Logloss.

Crossed full-minus-detached AUC is +0.00004607634386211146 but Logloss is worse by 0.00012588645933467313. The pairing-by-gradient interaction is +0.0003522827278239493 AUC and -0.00019906718446688343 Logloss. Alignment still wins under either gradient rule and under raw products.

Both detached checkpoints report identical same-state full/detached products and logits (max absolute differences zero). Candidate diagnostics show zero padding mass, zero empty summary, weight-sum errors <=1.1920928955078125e-7 and unit-product norm errors <=1.7881393432617188e-7. No floor cases occur in 60,475 visible events among the first 512 impressions. Backward correctness and population absence of floor cases are not measured.

Full aligned is not uniformly best. In the highest training-frequency slice (1,004,912 impressions, 33,140 positives), its AUC 0.6365456862 is below detached 0.6365801374 and raw 0.6367937224. In history_17_64 (157,391 impressions, 6,311 positives), full aligned loses both metrics to raw. Empty-history changes have only 310 positives and zero direct history summaries; shared training effects are plausible.

All detailed interaction models have 17,130,275 parameters (17,078,688 embedding; 51,587 dense). Full-unit peak GPU bytes are 832,739,328 versus 800,846,848 detached. Their training times span about 521-529 seconds. Single-run timing and memory are observations; no equal-compute frontier or production throughput gain is established.

observations.observation: All 25 supplied trajectories succeeded operationally. Full and half count correction both lose DIN AUC. Half pooling improves on ordinary pooling but remains below DIN; full pooling correction loses AUC. These are scientific negatives or limited successes, not execution failures. No hidden failures are inferred.

The joint round-3 restriction gains 0.001162954694291618 AUC over its ordinary adapter. Cross-field removal alone nearly matches it. Context and cross-field restrictions interact; individual removal gains are not additive. Same-seed round-4 consistency and the round-6 raw bridge do not eliminate the small ordinary-adapter versus original-DIN offset.

Normalized aligned full-gradient remains the validation incumbent: AUC 0.6149816911798147 and Logloss 0.19656340759133067. It exceeds raw aligned by 0.0004876567525730069 AUC. Alignment beats crossed replacement under raw, unit-full and unit-detached rules at this seed.

Latest identity-gradient AUC is 0.6135629923558267; tangent-gradient AUC is 0.6140637917286534. Both lose AUC and Logloss to the incumbent. Tangent beats identity AUC but has worse Logloss; detached beats tangent AUC and Logloss. All remain seed-42 observations.

The aligned four-arm AUC ordering is full > detached > tangent > identity. Inverse-norm scaling gains 0.0010203397523019797 without projection and 0.0009178994511612748 with projection. Projection gains 0.0005007993728267657 without scaling and 0.00039835907168606077 with scaling. AUC interaction is -0.0001024403011407049.

Logloss does not follow the same factor ordering: projection without scaling worsens loss by 0.00002937708836051045, while projection with scaling improves it by 0.0000731807251322103. Scaling without projection changes loss by +0.00000029026315062630204, with no precision estimate; scaling with projection improves it by 0.00010226755034209445. Loss interaction is -0.00010255781349272075.

Both new arms report same-state full/surrogate product and logit max absolute differences of zero. On the first 512 validation impressions: 508 nonempty, 4 empty, 60,475 valid visible events, zero sampled floored events; zero padding mass and empty summaries. These are candidate-supplied forward checks, not independently verified backward tests.

The incumbent is not uniformly best across slices. Tangent slightly wins both metrics in history_1_16 (41,805 samples, 1,444 positives); raw wins both in history_17_64 (157,391 samples, 6,311 positives) and highest training-frequency group (1,004,912 samples, 33,140 positives). Empty-history AUC and Logloss ranks differ despite zero direct summaries.

All detailed history interaction arms have 17,130,275 parameters. Latest identity/tangent training times are 500.0755941569805/506.70840303599834 seconds and peak GPU bytes 800,977,920/834,704,896; full is 524.601099088788 seconds and 832,739,328 bytes. Inference is about 179k-180k examples/second for these three runs, including causal gathering, batch size 4096. No equal-compute or serving advantage is established.
